 Order
The petitioner is the accused in Crime No.1973/2023 of Ernakulam Town North Police Station.

The offences alleged against him are under Sections 376(2)(n), 313, 323, 308 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2.
The prosecution case is that the accused committed rape on the de facto complainant by giving her the false promise of marriage.
It is stated that the de facto complainant had undergone sexual intercourse with the petitioner/accused on various occasions starting from 2020 November till 22 nd June 2023 at various places.
On all such occasions, the de facto complainant is said to have extended her consent believing the offer of marriage made by the petitioner.

There are also allegations to the effect that the petitioner had physically assaulted the de facto complainant and administered tablets for aborting her pregnancy when she got conceived from the petitioner.

3. In the present petition, the petitioner would contend that none of the offences alleged against him in this case are attracted since the de facto complainant had voluntarily indulged in sexual 2025:KER:40325 relationship with the petitioner.

It is also stated that the petitioner has married the de facto complainant, and hence there is absolutely no basis for the allegation that the petitioner committed rape by giving her false promise of marriage.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, learned counsel for the 3rd respondent, and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.
5. Annexure-A2 is the copy of the marriage certificate issued by the Marriage Officer, Cheriyanad,
Alappuzha.
Annexure-A2 marriage certificate would reveal that the petitioner married the de facto complainant on 20.10.2023, in accordance with the provisions of the Special Marriage Act, 1954.
6. The de facto complainant has also filed an affidavit in respect of the above marriage with the petitioner and has stated that she has no subsisting grievance as against the petitioner.

7. The learned Public Prosecutor, on instructions, submitted that the de facto complainant had given statement to the Investigating Officer to the effect that the petitioner had married her, and that they are living together as husband and wife.

8. It is apparent from the aforesaid facts and 2025:KER:40325 circumstances of the case that the allegation against the petitioner about indulging in sexual intercourse with the de facto complainant by giving false promise of marriage, is totally baseless.

Since the petitioner had already married the de facto complainant, and both of them are leading a peaceful family life, it cannot be said that the consent, which the de facto complainant had extended for having sexual relationship with the petitioner, was vitiated due to misconception of facts or any fraudulent act.
Therefore, this is a fit case where the proceedings against the petitioner have to be terminated.

Since no offence as alleged in Annexure-A1 FIR are attracted, the prayer of the petitioner to quash the proceedings against him,

2 has to be allowed.
